title: Reconciled by the Blood of His Cross
speaker: Jonathan Baird
summary: Without Jesus we would remain guilty before God and unable even to respond. He is the one mediator who lays his hand on us both.
exhortation: Our focus this morning is verse 20: "and through him to reconcile to himself all things, whether on earth or in heaven, making peace by the blood of his cross."

If Jesus had not come and reconciled us to God by his blood, we would be utterly lost. We would remain guilty before God, powerless to change and unable even to respond. Listen to Job: "For he is not a man, as I am, that I might answer him, that we should come to trial together. There is no arbiter between us, who might lay his hand on us both. Let him take his rod away from me, and let not dread of him terrify me."

If Jesus had not become a man, lived the perfect life and died willingly in our place, there would be no way for us to be reconciled to God. That is why we can be saved only through Jesus. As Paul says in 1 Timothy 2:5-6, "For there is one God, and there is one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus, who gave himself as a ransom for all."

So this morning, let's marvel at the loving plan of the Father and the love of Jesus, who came and laid down his life so that we could be reconciled to God, and let's remind ourselves how awesome this grace toward us is.
prayer: Lord, we are so grateful that you will come again. Because of your grace and the blood shed on the cross, we can look forward to being with you in body, raised to be with you forever, celebrating your grace and mercy for all eternity.
Fill us with strength from these truths today as we go about our day, and remind us that you are with us every step of the way. In Jesus' name.
